'''''Erophaca''''' is a [[monotypic genus]] of the tribe [[Galegeae]]. Its only species, '''''Erophaca baetica''''', is a perennial plant distributed in disjunct populations in the [[Mediterranean Region]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.floraiberica.es/floraiberica/texto/pdfs/07_29%20Erophaea.pdf |title=Erophaca Boiss |publisher=floraiberica.es |access-date=September 13, 2020}}</ref>

According to [[nrDNA]] [[Internal transcribed spacer|ITS]] analysis, ''Erophaca'' is [[monophyletic]] and related to the [[Astragalus (plant)|Astragalean]] clade. It is also [[Andromonoecy|andromonoecious]] (a rare [[sexual system]] among the [[angiosperms]] and a novelty for [[Old World]] [[Faboideae|papilionoid]] legumes).<ref>{{cite journal |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1111/j.1438-8677.2012.00648.x |title=Andromonoecy in an Old World Papilionoid legume, Erophaca baetica |author=R. Casimiro-Soriguer |author2=J. Herrera |author3=S. Talavera |journal=Plant Biology |year=2013 |volume=15 |issue=2 |pages=353–359 |doi=10.1111/j.1438-8677.2012.00648.x |pmid=22823201 |bibcode=2013PlBio..15..353C |access-date=September 13, 2020|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S105579031000093X |title=Phylogeny and genetic structure of Erophaca (Leguminosae), a East–West Mediterranean disjunct genus from the Tertiary |year=2010 |publisher=RamónCasimiro-Soriguer et al. |doi=10.1016/j.ympev.2010.02.025 |access-date=September 13, 2020|last1=Casimiro-Soriguer |first1=Ramón |last2=Talavera |first2=María |last3=Balao |first3=Francisco |last4=Terrab |first4=Anass |last5=Herrera |first5=Javier |last6=Talavera |first6=Salvador |journal=Molecular Phylogenetics and Evolution |volume=56 |issue=1 |pages=441–450 |pmid=20219686 |bibcode=2010MolPE..56..441C |url-access=subscription }}</ref>

''Erophaca baetica'' has two [[subspecies]] distributed at [[Disjunct distribution|opposite ends]] of the Mediterranean region:

*''E. baetica subsp. baetica'': Native to the southern half of the [[Iberian Peninsula]] (Portugal and Spain) and Northwest Africa ([[Morocco]] and [[Algeria]]).

*''E. baetica subsp. orientalis'': Native to the Eastern Mediterranean ([[Greece]], [[Turkey]], [[Cyprus]] and [[Lebanon]]).

Some populations in Algeria were found to be [[Hybrid (biology)|hybrids]] of the two subspecies.
